audit.reasoning: (1) Both deciding quotations verified verbatim at the stated places: French c.1979 p.7 sec. 3.3 (page scan) and Rappa 1996 secs. 2.4/3 (extracted text of the PDF we hold). (2) The classification rests on two primary SIL phonology manuscripts (c.1979, 1996) with minimal pairs; short, but first-hand. The most authoritative published treatment, Newell 2006 Romblomanon Dictionary front matter sec. 1.1.3, was downloaded now (Webonary/the Internet Archive) and states: phonemic length 'with accompanying stress' on the penult of some words, final stress on words without length, minimal pairs bitu^un/bitu:^un, maguyang/magu:yang, ^unu/^u:nu, and rightward length shift under suffixation. This is the standard Bisayan analysis and maps onto our lexical coding exactly (penult vs ultima prominence unpredictable per lexeme); it also matches the record's the primary-stress rule note that French calls the contrast stress while Rappa calls it length. sources.quote: General West-Visayan note only: 'In West Visayan languages stress is important in this same way, and in other instances even more important to meaning ... some words, though sounding very much the same, have no relationship of meaning; yet they differ in pronunciation by stress ... N.B. unless a word receives an accent in this book, it will be accented on the second last syllable which is most common in Philippine languages.' No Romblomanon-specific minimal pairs.

sources.citation: Law, Rence & Phyllis Rappa. 2006. Request for Working Orthography for Romblomanon (4th proposal), SIL Philippines, dated 22 Nov 2006, 6 pp. romblomanon.net upload.
sources.quote: 'Stress is phonemic: e.g. pilá 'how much?' and píla 'queue in a line'. Consonant and vowel lengths are not phonemic; no contrasts have been found. Length is not symbolized. Stress is symbolized only when necessary, which is rare.' (Same SIL team as Rappa 1996, now labelling the lexical contrast 'stress' rather than 'length'.)

sources.quote: 'Length is a phonemic feature of Romblomanon. It occurs, with accompanying stress, on the penult (second to last syllable) of some words. The last vowel of words with no discernable length is commonly stressed. Stress is recognized as an articulatory feature of length. Length has an important function in Romblomanon and is consistently signaled in this dictionary (e.g., bitu^un 'a butong tree'; bitu:^un 'star'; maguyang 'older sibling'; magu:yang 'mature, old'; ^unu 'what does someone do?'; ^u:nu 'one').'
